get.description: One keyset-paginated page of variants. All nine filters combine conjunctively. A model or family slug naming nothing is a 404; a reference code no vocabulary carries, a year outside 1900-2100, an unsupported sort, and a malformed cursor are 400. The reported limit is the one applied, after defaulting to 50 and capping at 200. Summaries carry identity and lineage only; no specification measurement appears, canonical or pending.

parameters.description: Parent model slug.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Grandparent family slug.

parameters.name: variant_type
parameters.description: Variant type code.

parameters.name: service_status
parameters.description: Service status code.

parameters.name: landing_gear_type
parameters.description: Landing gear type code.

parameters.name: propulsion_category
parameters.description: Propulsion category code.

parameters.name: country_of_origin
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code, upper case.

parameters.name: is_in_production
parameters.description: Whether the variant is recorded as in production.

parameters.name: produced_in_year
parameters.description: Variants whose production run covered this year. A run with no end year is still in production and is included.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. slug_asc is the only supported value.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 50; values above 200 are capped to 200, and the applied value is reported as the response's limit. A limit of 0 is refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous page's next_cursor. Clients must not construct or interpret one.

CatalogEntryResponse.description:
One lookup row on the wire.

`description` is omitted when the row has none, or when the catalog's table
has no such column at all -- the rule the measurement representation follows,
and deliberately the opposite of `PageResponse::next_cursor`, which is `null`
on a final page so a paging client can read the member rather than test for
it. Nothing polls a catalog for a missing description.

code.description: The stable machine code, as `aircraft_ref.lookup_code` spells it.

DecimalStringResponse.description:
A `NUMERIC` value on the wire: always a JSON string, never a JSON number.

The published `pattern` is the grammar and deliberately not the capacity:
`DecimalString` bounds digits at what `PostgreSQL` can store, but
republishing those five-digit quantifiers as a `maxLength` would put a
storage detail in the public contract, which the pull-request `oasdiff`
gate would then freeze.

FamilyDetailResponse.description:
One family, whole.

The summary's members are repeated rather than nested or flattened, which is
what `AGENTS.md` asks of HTTP DTOs: explicit mappings of the application
types, not structural reuse of them. `name_aliases` is always present,
possibly empty, because [`FamilyDetail`] already collapsed a NULL array to
an empty one.

FamilySort.description:
Which order a caller asked for.

A closed enum rather than a string, so `?sort=name_desc` is refused by the
query deserialization that already refuses `?limit=abc`.

FamilySummaryResponse.description: One family as a collection row.

manufacturer.description:
The manufacturing organisation's own slug, absent when the family records
no manufacturer.

slug.description: The stable public identifier, as `aircraft_ref.slug_text` spells it.

MeasurementConditionsResponse.description:
The conditions a measurement was taken under. Present only when the source
supplied at least one; the domain constructor drops an empty set.

isa_deviation_c.description: Deviation from ISA in degrees Celsius.

MeasurementResponse.description:
One measured fact.

Fields are private and the type is built only through [`From`], so no caller
can assemble a response the domain constructor would have refused. Raw and
canonical units are independent members because conversion changes the unit:
a raw value in `METERS` has a canonical counterpart in `FT`.

is_canonical.description:
Whether this row is the one served through the canonical read model.
Absent for a fact table that carries no such column at all; `false` says
only that the row is unpublished, never why.

raw_unit_code.description:
Absent when the metric is dimensionless, which is the only reason an
applicable unit is ever missing.

ModelDetailResponse.description:
One model, whole.

The summary's members are repeated rather than nested or flattened, which is
what `AGENTS.md` asks for in keeping HTTP DTOs explicit mappings of the
application types instead of structural reuse of them. `name_aliases` is
always present, possibly empty, because [`ModelDetail`] already collapsed a
NULL array to an empty one and a client should not have to decide again.

ModelSort.description:
Which order a caller asked for.

A closed enum rather than a string, so `?sort=name_desc` is refused by the
same query deserialization that already refuses `?limit=abc` -- the `400`
the acceptance criteria require of an unsupported sort, with no comparison
of this module's own.

ModelSummaryResponse.description: One model as a collection row.

slug.description: The stable public identifier, as `aircraft_ref.slug_text` spells it.

PageResponse_FamilySummaryResponse.description:
One page on the wire.

`next_cursor` is serialized as `null` on a final page rather than omitted,
because the accepted decision says "Empty and final pages return a null next
cursor" -- the opposite of the omit-when-absent rule the measurement
representation follows, and deliberate: a client polling for more pages
reads the member rather than testing for its presence.

`limit` is the bound actually applied, which is not always the one asked
for: `PageLimit::from_requested` substitutes the default when none was sent
and caps anything above the ceiling. Issue #43 requires the variant
collection to report it, and it is on this shared envelope rather than on
that one endpoint so all three collections answer the same shape. Adding a
member is the compatible addition `docs/architecture/http_v1_decisions.md`
allows within `/v1`.

limit.description:
The page bound this response was built with, after defaulting and
capping.

items.description:
One variant as a collection row.

Wider than the family and model rows because a variant is what a client
compares, which is the reasoning [`VariantSummary`] records. Every member is
an `aircraft_core.variants` column or its parent model's slug; none is a
measurement.

slug.description: The stable public identifier, as `aircraft_ref.slug_text` spells it.

limit.description:
The page bound this response was built with, after defaulting and
capping.

PowerSettingResponse.description:
The published spelling of an engine setting.

The variant names are Rust's; the `rename` values are the literals
`chk_pm_power_setting` allows in
`database/migrations/008_performance_metrics_conditions.sql`, which is why
three of them are not valid Rust identifiers.

instance.description:
The specific occurrence this problem describes.

Required, because `/ready` has published one since it shipped and
`oasdiff` fails the build on `response-property-became-optional`. A route
names itself with a borrowed constant, a perimeter refusal owns the path
it refused, and `Cow` is what lets one required field be both.

required_scope.description:
The scope required by the refused operation. Present only on an
authorization problem, and absent rather than null everywhere else.

type.description:
A URI reference identifying the problem type. Relative by design: it
resolves against the request URL, so no environment has to agree on a
hostname for the link to be correct.

RequiredScope.description: The scope the caller's credential is missing.

SurfaceTypeResponse.description:
The published spelling of a runway surface, from `chk_pm_surface_type` in
the same migration.

UnitCodeResponse.description:
A measurement-unit code on the wire, in the shape
`aircraft_ref.lookup_code` requires of every seeded code.
